summary: Repaired node1’s reconciliation job with a nonblocking kernel lock and exact ledger checks. Concurrent, interruption-recovery, idempotency, and restart-persistence tests passed. RHEL 7.9 and kernel 3.10.0-1160 remain unchanged.
actions_performed: Updated bin/reconcile to acquire an exclusive flock before reading pending.tsv.
Added a clear stderr message and exit status 75 when another invocation owns the job.
Verified an interrupted owner releases the lock automatically.
Processed B101 and B102 while preserving B100; all appear exactly once.
Restarted node1 safely and verified the changed boot identity, recovered services, script, and ledger.

evidence.requirement: Only one invocation processes pending.tsv and contention has a clear result
evidence.summary: Installed the nonblocking flock implementation; the concurrent caller returned 75 with an explicit already-running message.

evidence.requirement: Each batch ID reaches ledger.tsv once while existing entries are preserved
evidence.summary: B100, B101, and B102 each had count 1. A subsequent run left the ledger SHA-256 unchanged.

evidence.requirement: An interrupted invocation does not permanently block later work
evidence.summary: The active owner was terminated with ledger.tsv still containing only B100; the following invocation succeeded and processed B101 and B102.
Used the platform-installed util-linux flock 2.23.2. RHEL 7.9 and kernel 3.10.0-1160 were retained across the restart.

Baseline boot ID was 325732f1-bc39-4512-b05e-397f42060246; reboot was acknowledged; post-restart boot ID changed to 20bd8210-2afa-4615-ab29-e458c31120ff. The system and crond recovered, the script checksum persisted, reconciliation returned 0, and every ledger ID remained present exactly once.
